outputs.L3:
The invention relates to integrated modular display panels, and more particularly to a modular display panel structure suitable for use in LED display systems requiring efficient heat dissipation, compact integration, and environmental protection.

The modular display panel includes a shell formed at least partially from a first thermally conductive material. The shell defines an internal space in which a printed circuit board is disposed. The printed circuit board serves as a supporting and electrical interconnection structure for components of the display panel.

A plurality of light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are mounted on a first side of the printed circuit board. These LEDs are arranged to form the visible display surface of the modular panel. A driver circuit is electrically coupled to the LEDs from a second side of the printed circuit board, opposite the first side. The driver circuit controls operation of the LEDs, including the selective activation and modulation of the LEDs to generate images, video, or other visual information.

The modular display panel further includes a power supply unit configured to provide electrical power to the LEDs and associated driver circuitry. The printed circuit board is positioned between the power supply unit and the LEDs, thereby enabling a compact integrated arrangement in which the power supply unit, driver circuit, printed circuit board, and LEDs are assembled within or in association with the shell.

To improve thermal performance, a second thermally conductive material is provided between the power supply unit and an outer back side of the display panel. This second thermally conductive material facilitates heat transfer away from the power supply unit toward the rear exterior of the panel, reducing heat accumulation within the module. In combination with the first thermally conductive material of the shell, the structure promotes effective dissipation of heat generated by the LEDs, driver circuit, and power supply unit.

The display side of the modular panel is covered by a protective waterproof structure. This waterproof structure protects the LEDs and other internal components from moisture, dust, and other environmental contaminants while allowing light emitted by the LEDs to pass through. As a result, the integrated modular display panel provides a durable, compact, and thermally efficient construction suitable for indoor or outdoor display applications.
outputs.L4:
An integrated modular display panel is provided for use in LED display systems, information boards, advertising displays, architectural lighting displays, and other applications requiring durable and reliable visual output. The display panel includes a thermally conductive shell that forms at least part of the supporting body of the module. The shell may be made from aluminum, an aluminum alloy, magnesium alloy, thermally conductive composite material, or another material capable of efficiently transferring heat away from internal electronic components. By integrating the heat-dissipation function into the panel structure itself, the display module can maintain a compact form while reducing the need for additional external heat sinks or bulky cooling assemblies.

A printed circuit board is arranged within or against the thermally conductive shell. A plurality of light-emitting diodes are mounted on the printed circuit board to form the display surface or pixel array of the panel. The LEDs may be arranged in rows and columns, in pixel clusters, or in any other suitable configuration depending on the desired resolution, brightness, and display format. The printed circuit board provides electrical interconnection for the LEDs and may also include conductive traces, thermal vias, insulating layers, and mounting regions that facilitate both electrical performance and heat transfer.

A driver circuit is incorporated into the modular panel to control operation of the LEDs. The driver circuit may regulate current supplied to the LEDs, control brightness, manage scanning or addressing of pixel groups, and receive display data from an external controller or adjacent panel module. In some embodiments, the driver circuit is mounted on the same printed circuit board as the LEDs. In other embodiments, it is mounted on a separate circuit board positioned within the shell. Integrating the driver circuit into the panel module simplifies installation, reduces external wiring, and allows each module to operate as a self-contained display unit or as part of a larger tiled display assembly.

A power supply is also arranged within the panel structure. The power supply may convert incoming electrical power into one or more regulated voltages suitable for the LEDs and driver circuitry. By locating the power supply inside the modular panel, the design reduces the complexity of system-level power distribution and allows the panel to be connected more easily to external power and control sources. The internal arrangement of the power supply, driver circuit, and LED circuit board may be selected to promote efficient heat conduction to the thermally conductive shell while maintaining electrical safety and operational stability.

During operation, heat generated by the LEDs, driver circuit, and power supply is transferred through the printed circuit board and associated thermal interfaces to the thermally conductive shell. The shell then dissipates the heat to the surrounding environment through conduction, convection, and radiation. This integrated thermal management approach helps lower the operating temperature of the LEDs and electronic components, thereby improving luminous efficiency, reducing thermal stress, and extending service life. The structure is particularly suitable for high-brightness LED displays or outdoor display panels that must operate for long periods under varying environmental conditions.

The display side of the panel is protected by a waterproof protective structure. The protective structure may include a transparent or translucent protective cover, sealing layer, encapsulant, gasket, waterproof coating, or a combination of these elements. The protective structure is arranged over or around the LED display surface to prevent water, dust, moisture, and other contaminants from reaching the LEDs and circuit board. In some embodiments, the protective structure is bonded, sealed, or mechanically fastened to the shell so as to form a weather-resistant enclosure. The protective material may be selected to provide high light transmission, impact resistance, ultraviolet resistance, and long-term environmental durability.

The modular display panel may further include mounting features, electrical connectors, signal interfaces, alignment structures, sealing grooves, or fastening portions that allow multiple panels to be assembled together into a larger display. Each module may be independently replaceable, which simplifies maintenance and reduces downtime. The integrated construction also helps improve mechanical strength and consistency between modules, making the display system easier to install and more reliable in use.

Through the combination of a thermally conductive shell, an internally arranged LED printed circuit board, integrated driver circuitry, an internal power supply, and a waterproof protective display-side structure, the panel provides a compact and robust LED display module. The design improves heat dissipation, protects sensitive electronic components from environmental exposure, reduces wiring complexity, and supports stable, durable, and reliable LED panel operation in both indoor and outdoor environments.

**The Embodiments of LEDs**

The embodiments of LEDs have transformed modern lighting by offering efficient, durable, and versatile illumination solutions. LEDs, or light-emitting diodes, are used in countless applications, from household lamps and streetlights to vehicle displays, smartphones, and medical devices. Their compact size and low energy consumption make them ideal for both everyday and specialized uses.

In different embodiments, LEDs may be arranged in strips, panels, bulbs, or integrated circuits, depending on the desired brightness, color, and function. Some embodiments focus on improving heat dissipation, while others enhance color accuracy, flexibility, or smart-control features. The continued development of LEDs has made lighting more sustainable, cost-effective, and adaptable to modern technology needs.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a brief “Embodiments of the present invention” section describing a modular display panel where LEDs are mounted on one side of a PCB, the driver connects from the opposite side, and thermal materials conduct heat to the back of the panel.
counterfactuals.output:
### Embodiments of the Present Invention

In some embodiments, a modular display panel includes a printed circuit board (PCB) having a front side and an opposite rear side. A plurality of light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are mounted on the front side of the PCB to define a display surface. One or more driver circuits or driver modules are electrically connected to the PCB from the rear side, thereby allowing control signals and power to be supplied to the LEDs without occupying space on the display surface.

In certain embodiments, the PCB includes conductive vias, thermal vias, metal layers, or other heat-transfer structures configured to transfer heat generated by the LEDs from the front side of the PCB toward the rear side. A thermal interface material may be disposed between the rear side of the PCB and a rear support plate, chassis, heat sink, or back cover of the panel. The thermal interface material may include a thermally conductive pad, grease, adhesive, gap filler, or phase-change material.

In some embodiments, heat generated by the LEDs is conducted through the PCB and the thermal interface material to the back of the modular display panel, where the heat may be dissipated by the rear support structure or an attached heat sink. This arrangement can improve thermal management while maintaining a compact modular construction and permitting the driver components to be accessed or serviced from the rear side of the panel.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a concise patent disclosure summary for an integrated modular display panel assembly with internal power supply, PCB, LEDs, rear heat dissipation, and a waterproof front/display side.
counterfactuals.output:
## Patent Disclosure Summary: Integrated Modular Display Panel Assembly

An integrated modular display panel assembly is disclosed for use in indoor or outdoor electronic display systems. The assembly includes a self-contained display module having a front display side that is waterproof or weather-resistant, and a rear side configured for heat dissipation and service access.

The panel assembly comprises a housing or frame supporting a printed circuit board (PCB), a plurality of light-emitting diodes (LEDs) mounted on or electrically coupled to the PCB, and an internal power supply disposed within the module. The internal power supply converts incoming electrical power to operating power for the PCB and LEDs, reducing the need for external power conversion components and simplifying installation.

The front/display side includes a transparent, translucent, or optically exposed protective layer, sealing structure, coating, gasket, potting material, or encapsulation that prevents water ingress while allowing emitted light to pass through. The waterproof front construction protects the LEDs and PCB from moisture, dust, and environmental contaminants.

The rear side of the module includes heat dissipation features, such as a thermally conductive back plate, fins, vents, heat spreaders, metal housing portions, or other thermal pathways. Heat generated by the LEDs, PCB, and internal power supply is transferred rearward and dissipated away from the waterproof display face.

The assembly may be formed as a modular tile or panel configured to connect mechanically and electrically with adjacent modules to create a larger display screen. Each module may include electrical connectors, mounting features, alignment structures, sealing interfaces, and control signal connections. The integrated configuration enables rapid installation, replacement, and maintenance while improving environmental protection, thermal performance, and system reliability.

Potential advantages include reduced external wiring, simplified assembly, improved waterproofing at the display surface, enhanced rear-side cooling, compact construction, and modular scalability for large-format LED displays.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in patent application language, one embodiment of a modular LED panel having a thermally conductive housing, PCB disposed between LEDs and a power supply, driver circuitry coupled through the PCB, and a protective waterproof display surface.
counterfactuals.output:
In one embodiment, a modular light emitting diode (LED) panel includes a thermally conductive housing defining an interior cavity and a front opening. The housing may be formed from aluminum, an aluminum alloy, or another thermally conductive material and may be configured to function as a heat sink for heat generated during operation of the LED panel.

A plurality of LEDs is disposed adjacent the front opening of the housing and arranged to emit light through a display surface of the panel. A printed circuit board (PCB) is positioned within the housing between the plurality of LEDs and a power supply. The PCB includes conductive traces configured to electrically interconnect the LEDs with driver circuitry and to distribute power and control signals to the LEDs. In some implementations, the LEDs are mounted directly to a first side of the PCB, while the power supply is positioned on, adjacent to, or thermally coupled with an opposing side of the PCB.

Driver circuitry is electrically coupled to the plurality of LEDs through the PCB. The driver circuitry may include one or more LED driver integrated circuits, current regulation components, voltage conversion components, dimming control components, and/or communication interfaces for receiving control signals from an external controller. The driver circuitry is configured to regulate electrical power delivered to the LEDs and to control illumination of the LEDs according to received power and/or data signals.

A protective display surface is disposed over the plurality of LEDs at the front opening of the housing. The protective display surface may include a transparent or translucent cover, lens, encapsulant, potting material, polymer layer, glass layer, or combinations thereof. The protective display surface is sealed relative to the housing to inhibit ingress of water, dust, or other contaminants into the interior cavity, thereby providing a waterproof or water-resistant front display surface. In certain embodiments, a gasket, adhesive, overmold, sealant, or peripheral weld may be provided between the protective display surface and the housing to establish a fluid-tight seal.

The housing, PCB, LEDs, driver circuitry, power supply, and protective display surface may be configured as a self-contained module. The module may include one or more electrical connectors for detachable connection to adjacent LED panels, a support frame, or an external power and control system, thereby permitting a plurality of the modular LED panels to be assembled into a larger display or lighting array. Heat generated by the LEDs and/or power supply may be conducted through the PCB and into the thermally conductive housing for dissipation to the surrounding environment, while the protective display surface maintains environmental isolation of the LEDs and associated circuitry.
